item.title: Remember, stop, try: -ing or to + verb?
item.explanation_text: Some verbs can be followed by -ing or by to + infinitive, but the meaning changes. remember / forget + -ing = a memory of something you did earlier: I remember locking the door. remember / forget + to = something you need to do: Remember to lock the door. stop + -ing = no longer do something: He stopped smoking. stop + to = stop one activity in order to do another: He stopped to buy water. try + -ing = do something as an experiment to see if it helps: Try restarting the laptop. try + to = make an effort to do something difficult: I tried to open the window, but it was stuck. regret + -ing = be sorry about something in the past: I regret leaving so early. regret + to = a formal way to give bad news: We regret to inform you that the flight has been cancelled. go on + -ing = continue the same activity; go on + to = do something new next.
item.contrast_text: Compare: I'll never forget meeting you (a memory of the past). Don't forget to meet Daniel at the airport (a task for the future).
item.common_error_pattern: Choosing -ing or to + verb by sound rather than meaning, for example 'I stopped to smoke' when you mean you gave it up.

examples.bad: Please remember sending me the file tonight.
examples.good: Please remember to send me the file tonight.

examples.bad: My father stopped to smoke ten years ago.
examples.good: My father stopped smoking ten years ago.

examples.bad: We regret informing you that your application was unsuccessful.
examples.good: We regret to inform you that your application was unsuccessful.

examples.bad: I'll never forget to visit Khiva for the first time.
examples.good: I'll never forget visiting Khiva for the first time.
